concepts.label: Clinical Informatics — Definition
concepts.summary: The application of informatics and IT to deliver healthcare services and to support and enhance clinical care. Anchored in the AMIA core competencies.

concepts.label: AMIA Core Competencies
concepts.summary: The four practice domains the field has agreed on: fundamentals; clinical decision making and care process improvement; health information systems; leadership and managing change. Tracks the ABPM exam outline.

concepts.label: Bioinformatics vs Clinical Informatics
concepts.summary: Bioinformatics: molecular/cellular unit of analysis, bench scientists as customers. Clinical informatics: patient encounter as unit, clinicians as customers. Disambiguate boundary cases by primary unit of analysis.

concepts.label: Public Health Informatics
concepts.summary: Population-level informatics: surveillance, registries, vital statistics, outbreak detection. Customer is the health department, not the bedside clinician.

concepts.label: Consumer Health Informatics
concepts.summary: Person-level informatics outside the clinical encounter: patient portals, wearables, PHRs, symptom checkers. Customer is the patient/caregiver.

concepts.label: Sociotechnical System
concepts.summary: A system whose behavior is determined jointly by technology and the humans, processes, organizations, and incentives wrapped around it. The unit of analysis for a clinical informaticist is always the system-in-context.

concepts.label: DIKW Hierarchy
concepts.summary: Data → Information → Knowledge → Wisdom. Each level adds context or synthesis. Useful as a teaching device; misleading if taken as an architecture diagram, since wisdom is produced by humans, not pipelines.

concepts.label: Data vs Information
concepts.summary: Data is uninterpreted measurement. Information is data plus the context (who/what/when/where/units) that makes it interpretable. The data-to-information seam is what standards like LOINC, UCUM, and FHIR exist to enable.

concepts.label: Knowledge Representation
concepts.summary: The problem of getting general clinical knowledge (rules, guidelines, relationships) into a form a computer can apply to a specific patient. The entire subject of Module 4.

concepts.label: Structured vs Unstructured Data
concepts.summary: Structured: codified into discrete, queryable fields with standard vocabularies. Unstructured: free text, scanned documents, images. NLP attempts to bridge — always lossy because the writer was not writing for the parser.

concepts.label: Context of Interpretation
concepts.summary: The metadata and clinical situation required to interpret data correctly. The same number can mean different things for the same patient on different days.

concepts.label: Early HIS Systems
concepts.summary: Memorize the four-way mapping: COSTAR-MGH-outpatient; Technicon-Lockheed-ElCamino-firstHIS; HELP-Warner-Intermountain-CDS; VistA-VA-hardhats. Plus Regenstrief-IndianaUniversity-LOINC-INPC.

concepts.label: VistA
concepts.summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs' clinician-built EHR, developed by the underground 'hardhats' group beginning in the 1980s. Long the largest non-commercial EHR deployment in the world. Now being replaced at the VA by commercial Cerner.

concepts.label: Regenstrief Medical Record
concepts.summary: Started 1972 at Indiana University under Clement McDonald. The institutional ancestor of structured clinical data, LOINC, and the Indiana Network for Patient Care.

concepts.label: HELP System
concepts.summary: Health Evaluation through Logical Processing. Developed at LDS Hospital under Homer Warner. The first major system to integrate CDS into routine workflow. Lineage runs to modern Intermountain Healthcare.

concepts.label: Meaningful Use
concepts.summary: The Medicare/Medicaid EHR incentive program created by HITECH (2009), administered by CMS, with EHR certification by ONC. Three stages. Drove U.S. hospital basic-EHR adoption from ~10% (2008) to >90% (2017). Transitioned to Promoting Interoperability under MIPS.

concepts.label: HITECH Act
concepts.summary: Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health, part of the 2009 ARRA stimulus. Created Meaningful Use, expanded HIPAA breach notification, and reshaped the U.S. health IT landscape.

concepts.label: 21st Century Cures Act (history)
concepts.summary: Passed 2016. Among many other things, introduced the information blocking rule with eight specific exceptions. Operationalized by ONC; took full effect 2022. Detailed in Module 7.

concepts.label: Friedman's Fundamental Theorem
concepts.summary: (Person + Information Resource) > Person. The unit of evaluation is the partnership in context, not the resource in isolation. The single most-cited and most-violated principle in the field.

concepts.label: Human-plus-System Evaluation
concepts.summary: Friedman's framing applied: evaluate the human-plus-system partnership against the unassisted human, in the actual setting, on a metric that matters. Most published evaluations of clinical AI fail this test.

concepts.label: Augmentation vs Automation
concepts.summary: Augmentation keeps the human in the loop and is governed by Friedman's theorem. Automation removes the human and is governed by a different and harder set of evaluations — safety, liability, regulation.

concepts.label: Intervention Evaluation Checklist
concepts.summary: Six questions: who is the person? what is the baseline? what is the assisted version? is it better on a metric that matters? does the comparison hold in the real setting? is the gain worth the cost?

concepts.label: Informatics vs IT
concepts.summary: Clinical IT delivers and operates the technology layer. Clinical informatics makes the technology actually deliver clinical value in a sociotechnical system. Test ownership by asking what changes for the patient when the problem is solved.

concepts.label: Clinical IT Roles
concepts.summary: Servers, networks, identity, backup, DR, vendor management, security operations, deployment, ticket triage, hardware refresh, help desk. Real, hard, important, and not clinical informatics.

concepts.label: CMIO Role
concepts.summary: Chief Medical Information Officer. Physician leader of the clinical informatics function. Reporting line (CMO vs CIO vs CEO) determines what is structurally easy and hard.

concepts.label: Governance Structure
concepts.summary: How decisions about clinical informatics get made. Clarity of decision rights matters more than the exact org chart.

concepts.label: Reporting Relationships
concepts.summary: Trade-offs of CMIO reporting to CIO (operational closeness, risk of IT framing) vs CMO (clinical grounding, technical isolation) vs dual/peer (more complexity, more autonomy).
